note: Trainable: eligible for the fine-tune query distribution. Many chunks are Rolt's editorial commentary rather than Dionysius's text; probes drafted from passages that are clearly the treatise itself.

queries.query: Dionysius's image of many lamps burning in a single room, their light blending into one glow while each flame stays distinct, explaining how the divine persons are united yet differentiated
queries.note: The lamps-in-one-house simile for Undifference and Differentiation; 'wholly interpenetrating one another', 'by their distinctions united into one' paraphrased away.

queries.query: the Divine Names argument that evil has no real being of its own: it is only a weakness and lack of goodness, since the Good can no more produce what is bad than heat can produce cold
queries.note: Evil as privation in chapter 4; 'even as fire cannot cool us' recast as heat/cold, 'impotence and weakness and an inharmonious mingling' paraphrased away; the treatise's title kept as anchor.

queries.query: Dionysius on divine yearning as ecstatic: love carries lovers out of themselves so they belong to the beloved, and even the maker of all is drawn beyond himself toward his creatures
queries.note: The ecstasy of the Divine Yearning in chapter 4; 'not allowing them that are touched thereby to belong unto themselves', 'yearneth after all things ... through excess of Goodness' paraphrased away.

queries.query: why scripture gives God many titles drawn from his gifts and workings, though the Godhead itself stands beyond every name and description
queries.note: Chapter 1 on the Names as symbolic revelations of the Emanations; 'beneficent Emanations', the catalogue of scriptural titles, 'Nameless Goodness' paraphrased away.

queries.query: if everything flows from a single good source, where does evil come from
queries.note: The origin-of-evil problem chapter 4 wrestles with; zoroastrian, gnostic, vedantic and other material answers it too. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: do all things long to return to the source from which they came
queries.note: The circle of yearning from the Good back to the Good; the return-to-source motif is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
